## Data Acquisition and Preparation

```{r}


library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
  library(tidyverse)
  library(stringr)
  library(httr2)
  library(rvest)
  library(fs)
  
  state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
  
  dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
  
  fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
  
  if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
    BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
    RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
      req_url_path("electricity", 
                   "state", 
                   state_formatted) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
      ) |>   
      req_retry(
        max_tries = 4, 
      ) |>
      req_perform(file_name)
    
    resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
  }
  
  TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
    html_element("table") |> 
    html_table() |>
    mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
  
  if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
    TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
  }
  
  CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
    filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
    pull(Value) |> 
    str_replace_all(",", "") |>
    as.numeric()
  
  PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
    filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
    pull(Rank)
  
  RATE <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    as.numeric()
  
  GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    str_replace_all(",", "") |>
    as.numeric()
  
  data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
             primary_source        = PRIMARY,
             electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
             # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
             generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
             state                 = state, 
             abbreviation          = abbr
  )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()


load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)
  
  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")
  
  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
    
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
    cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
    stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
  }
  
  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }
  
  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()



load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)
  
  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")
  
  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
    
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` + `sum_ada_upt` + `sum_sponsored_service_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
    cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
    stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
  }
  
  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()

```

## Exploratory Analysis


1. The 5 states that have the most expensive retail electricity are listed in the graph below:
``` {r}
library(scales)


#1. Which 5 states have the most expensive retail electricity? (Graph)
library(ggplot2)
expensive_electricity <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  arrange(desc(electricity_price_MWh)) |> 
  head(5) 

ggplot(expensive_electricity, aes(x = state, y=electricity_price_MWh )) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Most Expensive Retail Electricity",
       subtitle = "Top five states and Electricity Price",
       x = "State",
       y = "Electricity Price per MWh")
  

```
It's not surprising to see Hawaii is the state with the most expensive electricity prices. It's far out in the Pacific Ocean, they use petroleum, and, after a quick search, the petroleum they rely on is imported. 
Another no surprise is California. After another search, electric companies in California invest heavily in wildfire prevention and maintaining aging infrastructure, and the costs of that are passed on to customers. It's no wonder why Pacific Gas & Electric customers (from Humboldt in NorCal to Santa Barbara in SoCal) are outraged at PG&E's audacity to increase prices despite their constant outages, having caused an explosion in San Bruno, CA in 2011, and causing wildfires.




The states with the dirtiest electricity mix are listed below:
```{r}
#2. Which 5 states have the ‘dirtiest’ electricity mix? (Table)
library(gt)

dirtiest <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  arrange(desc(CO2_MWh)) |> 
  head(5) |> select(-abbreviation)

dirtiest |> gt() |>
  tab_header(title="Dirtiest Electricity Mix") |>
  cols_label(
    primary_source = "Source",
    electricity_price_MWh  = "Electricity Price per MWh", 
    state = "State",
    generation_MWh = "Generation per MWh",
    CO2_MWh = "CO2 per MWh"
    
  )
  

```
Again another no big surprise that the states with the dirtiest mix are states that use coal. WV and KY are definitely the states that come to mind when thinking of coal mining. After a quick search, I discovered that Wyoming is the largest coal-producing state in the US and while Missouri is not currently a coal mining state, it was historically. And again Hawaii is there from their reliance on petroleum.



The three rarest primary energy sources in the US are listed below
```{r}


#4. What are the three rarest primary energy sources in the US? 
rarest_sources <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> 
  group_by(primary_source) |> 
  summarize(count = n()) |> 
  arrange(count) |> 
  head(3)
#What is the associated cost of electricity associated with each source and in what states are they used? (Table answer)
rarest_sources |> 
  inner_join(EIA_SEP_REPORT, join_by(primary_source)) |> 
  select(primary_source, electricity_price_MWh, state) |> 
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title="Rarest Primary Energy Sources") |>
  cols_label(
    primary_source = "Source",
    electricity_price_MWh  = "Electricity Price per MWh", 
    state = "State"
  )

```
It's not that surprising that hydroelectric is one of the rarest, as that seems to be more geographically-driven. I can't imagine the deserts or the mountainous areas to have a lot of hydroelectricity generation. 
I did some quick searches into Idaho and Vermont's usage of hydroelectric, and these states have dams and rivers that generate about 46% and 51% of each state's electricity respectively. And of course Oregon and Washington have tons fo rivers running through each state.
I **am** surprised that wind is rare, because wind in general is everywhere even the deserts in California. 
Another big surprise is the petroleum use in Hawaii. For a state surrounded by water and with so much ocean breezes, I'm surprised that wind and hydroelectric aren't utilized more. Or even solar. But I guess limited land space limits their capacity for wind farms.

The dataset also included data from US territories including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, and US Virgin Islands.
Of the 50 states, Wyoming had 0 public transit passenger miles. After doing some quick searching, Wyoming actually **does** have public transit, so that just means that the actual public transit miles were probably just not recorded for Wyoming.
The next state with the least public transit miles is South Dakota.
These numbers and states seems legitimate, as I don't believe these states are known for public transit, neither are they known for being environmentally friendly; but rather known for suburbs and rural areas that are only reachable by private vehicles.

## Task 6
```{r}

# Same code -> name mapping used in Task 2 (reuse for both tables)
mode_names <- c(HR = "Heavy Rail", 
                DR = "Demand Response", FB = "Ferryboat",
                MB = "Bus", SR = "Streetcar Rail", TB = "Trolleybus",
                VP = "Vanpool", CB = "Commuter Bus", RB = "Bus Rapid Transit",
                LR = "Light Rail", YR = "Hybrid Rail",
                MG = "Monorail / Automated Guideway", CR = "Commuter Rail",
                AR = "Alaska Railroad", TR = "Aerial Tramway",
                IP = "Inclined Plane", CC = "Cable Car")


# NTD_SERVICE: one row per agency + mode (sum over type of service)
service_by_mode <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(NTD_ID = as.numeric(NTD_ID),
         Mode   = coalesce(unname(mode_names[mode]), "Unknown")) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, Mode, AGENCY, state) |>
  summarize(total_upt           = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum_passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# Join on BOTH keys; relationship= errors out if any row still duplicates
energy_service <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  inner_join(service_by_mode,
             join_by(`NTD ID` == NTD_ID, Mode),
             relationship = "one-to-one")


# emissions Per UPT and per passenger miles
efficiency <- energy_service |>
  mutate(total_sum = rowSums(pick(starts_with("Gallons"),
                                  starts_with("Kilowatt"),
                                  starts_with("Kilograms"))),
         per_upt     = total_sum / total_upt,
         per_pass_mi = total_sum / sum_passenger_miles) |>
  filter(total_upt > 0, sum_passenger_miles > 0) |>
  select(AGENCY, Mode, state, per_upt, per_pass_mi)

efficiency

```





## Awards Metrics
There are two awards I want to give out: The greenest agencies, and the worst polluters. 

The Greenest Agencies are the ones that have the highest use of a combination of bio diesel, electric, and hydrogen. The Worst polluters are the opposite: these agencies use more non-renewable fuels (Bunker Fuel, Compressed natural Gas, Diesel, Ethanol, Gasoline, Kerosene, Liquified Natural Gas, and Liquified Petroleum Gas). 

I chose bio diesel, electric, and hydrogen to be the markers of "green" fuels because these are renewable and/or biodegradable fuel sources. I'm not familiar with fuel sources in general so I had to do some quick searches on each fuel source in this dataset to be more certain about the renewability of each source. 

It's in a similar vein as to how I chose Bunker Fuel, Compressed natural Gas, Diesel, Ethanol, Gasoline, Kerosene, Liquified Natural Gas, and Liquified Petroleum Gas to be the non-renewable, and thus, the "not green", fuel sources. While Bunker Fuel, Compressed natural Gas, Diesel, Gasoline, Liquified Natural Gas, and Liquified Petroleum Gas are obviously not "green", the "green-ness" Ethanol and Kerosene are more dependent on how these fuels are processed and produced (emissions from production), so I decided to put these into the same category as the other non green fuels.

```{r}
#highest use of a combination of bio diesel, electric, and hydrogen; 
# and the highest use of a combination of non green fuels
fuel_totals <- NTD_ENERGY |> mutate(`Green Fuels` = rowSums(across(c(
  `Gallons of Bio-Diesel`,
  `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`,
  `Kilograms of Hydrogen`
)), na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  mutate(`Not Green Fuels` = rowSums(across(c(
    `Gallons of Bunker Fuel`,
    `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`,
    `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` ,
    `Gallons of Ethanol` ,
    `Gallons of Gasoline`, 
    `Gallons of Kerosene`  ,
    `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`,
    `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`
  )), na.rm = TRUE))|>
  group_by(`Agency Name`) |> 
  select(`Agency Name`, Mode, `Green Fuels`, `Not Green Fuels`)
#fuel_totals
```


```{r}
greenest_agencies <- fuel_totals |>
  mutate(`Fuel Use Difference` = `Green Fuels` - `Not Green Fuels`) |>
  group_by(`Agency Name`) |> 
  select(`Agency Name`, Mode, `Green Fuels`, `Not Green Fuels`, `Fuel Use Difference`) |>
  arrange(desc(`Fuel Use Difference`)) |>
  mutate(`Green Fuels`=comma(`Green Fuels`), 
         `Not Green Fuels`=comma(`Not Green Fuels`), 
         `Fuel Use Difference`=comma(`Fuel Use Difference`))
greenest_agencies |> print(n=5)

greenest_agency <- greenest_agencies |> head(1) |> pull(`Agency Name`)
#greenest_agency

greenest_agency_green <- greenest_agencies |> head(1) |> pull(`Green Fuels`)
greenest_agency_not_green <- greenest_agencies |> head(1) |> pull(`Not Green Fuels`)
greenest_diff <- greenest_agencies |> head(1) |> pull(`Fuel Use Difference`)

```
The award for Greenest Agency goes to `{r} greenest_agency`, with a total of `{r} greenest_agency_green` gallons of green fuels used, and `{r} greenest_agency_not_green` gallons of not green fuels used. 



```{r}
least_green <- fuel_totals |>
  mutate(`Fuel Use Difference` = `Not Green Fuels` - `Green Fuels`) |>
  group_by(`Agency Name`) |> 
  select(`Agency Name`, Mode, `Green Fuels`, `Not Green Fuels`, `Fuel Use Difference`) |>
  arrange(desc(`Fuel Use Difference`)) |>
  mutate(`Green Fuels`=comma(`Green Fuels`), 
       `Not Green Fuels`=comma(`Not Green Fuels`), 
       `Fuel Use Difference`=comma(`Fuel Use Difference`))

worst_polluter <- least_green |> head(1)
#worst_polluter

polluter_green_use <- worst_polluter |> pull(`Green Fuels`)
polluter_not_green_use <- worst_polluter |> pull(`Not Green Fuels`)
polluter_diff <- worst_polluter |> pull(`Fuel Use Difference`)

```

The award for Worst Polluter goes to `{r} worst_polluter`, with only `{r} polluter_green_use` gallons of green fuels used and `{r} polluter_not_green_use` gallons of non green fuels used. With a difference of `{r} polluter_diff` gallons between green and non green fuels, `{r} worst_polluter` is the worst polluter because it uses much more non green fuels than green fuels.
